chapter: Chapter 6. Solids and the solid–liquid transition
title: Plasticity and brittleness

prose.text:
Many solids can approximately regain their original size and shape after a load is removed, provided that the temperature and loading conditions are suitable, the deformation is sufficiently small, and no damage or significant irreversible process has occurred.
This recoverable response is called elasticity;
deformation is a change in size or shape, and a load is an applied force.

Small deformation alone does not guarantee that every material will recover completely.
The response also depends on the material's state, the stress, meaning the internal force per unit area, and the observation time.

Many materials can also undergo plastic deformation under certain conditions.
Plastic deformation leaves a permanent change in size or shape after the load is removed.
Elasticity and plasticity describe how a material responds and whether its deformation is recoverable.
prose.source_text: 任何材料组成的物体，当形变很小时都象弹性体一样，当去掉负载时，它的大小和形状得到恢复. 同时，几乎所有的物体都可以在某种程度上产生塑性形变.

prose.text:
Different materials have different mechanical responses.
Rubber and some kinds of steel can show pronounced elastic behavior within their respective conditions and deformation ranges.

The original textbook gives steel that still obeys Hooke's law at a relative elongation, or tensile strain, of $\varepsilon=1\%$ as an example.
Relative elongation is the increase in length divided by the original length, and Hooke's law states that stress is proportional to strain in the linear elastic range.
This is the textbook's material example, not a common upper limit of linear elasticity for all steels.

The textbook also gives an example of rubber remaining elastic when $\varepsilon$ reaches several tens of percent.
A large recoverable deformation does not mean that stress remains proportional to deformation: rubber can show nonlinear elasticity, so the textbook's claim about Hooke's law cannot be applied generally to such large deformations.
This section calls these materials "elastic materials" to emphasize recoverability under appropriate conditions, not to guarantee linear behavior throughout all deformation ranges.
prose.source_text: 不同材料的力学性质是不同的. 象橡皮或钢这样的材料，当应力和形变比较大时，仍具有弹性性质. 例如，对于钢来说，直到 $\varepsilon=1\%$ 还满足胡克定律，而对于橡皮来说，直到 $\varepsilon$ 相当大，等于百分之几十时，还满足胡克定律. 因此，这些物体叫做弹性物体.

prose.text:
The original textbook uses wet clay, plastics, and lead as examples of materials that readily retain plastic deformation: in the states and loading conditions under discussion, their elastic deformation range may be small, and even a modest load may cause permanent deformation, so the textbook calls them "plastic materials."
This term is not a fixed classification of all plastics or lead materials.
Changes in temperature, material composition, loading rate, and load duration can change their elastic, plastic, or time-dependent responses.
prose.source_text: 湿的粘土、塑料或铅的弹性形变的范围是很小的. 不大的负载，就可以使它们产生塑性形变. 这些物体叫做塑性物体.
划分物体是弹性物体还是塑性物体，在很大程度上是有条件的. 同一种材料是弹性物体还是塑性物体，取决于所产生的应力. 例如，在应力很大时，钢具有塑性性质. 在用产生巨大压力的压制机中压钢件时，就广泛地应用了钢的塑性性质.

prose.text:
Temperature affects a material's mechanical behavior.
Under suitable hot-working conditions, steel or iron is usually easier to forge into shape than when cold.
This does not mean that any amount of deformation can be obtained without limits at high temperatures.

Forging, which shapes metal by applied forces, is an industrial process, not an activity that this lesson asks you to perform.
The original textbook gives cooling lead below $-100^\circ C$ as an example: lead that readily undergoes plastic deformation at room temperature can show a more pronounced elastic response at lower temperatures.
This value is retained as the textbook's illustration, not a precise transition temperature shared by all lead materials, and it does not guarantee that every load at low temperature produces only elastic deformation.
prose.source_text: 用铁锤很难把冷的钢或铁锻造成形. 但是，把它们加热到很高温度以后，用锻造工具很容易使它们具有任意的形变. 如果把铅冷却到 $-100^\circ C$ 以下，则在室温下为塑性的铅就明显地表现出弹性性质.

prose.text:
Brittleness describes behavior in which a material undergoes very little plastic deformation before fracture.
In this section's tensile examples, the specimens fracture when their total deformation is still small.
Glass objects and porcelain usually show pronounced brittleness and may break on impact even when dropped onto a hard floor from a modest height.

The original textbook also lists cast iron, marble, and amber as examples of brittle materials.
In the material states and loading conditions usually discussed, steel, copper, and lead often show greater plasticity or ductility, meaning the ability to undergo appreciable plastic elongation in tension before breaking, than those materials.
This comparison does not mean that steel, copper, and lead cannot undergo brittle fracture at any temperature or under any processing or loading conditions.
prose.source_text: 物体的所谓脆性，在实际上具有很大的意义. 如果物体在形变很小时就破裂了，则这个物体叫做脆的物体. 玻璃制品和瓷器是脆的：甚至从不太高的地方掉在地板上，它们就被摔碎. 生铁、大理石、琥珀也具有很大的脆性. 相反的，钢、铜、铅等不是脆的物体.

prose.text:
Graphs of tensile stress $\sigma$ against relative elongation $\varepsilon$ can be used to compare brittle fracture with fracture after substantial plastic elongation.
Figures 89 and 90 show the textbook's cast iron and steel specimens, respectively.
The comparison uses engineering stress and engineering strain, which refer to the original cross-sectional area and original gauge length, respectively.

Engineering stress is tensile force divided by that original area.
Engineering strain is elongation divided by the original gauge length, the initial length over which elongation is measured.
These quantities must not be mixed with local true stress, which uses the local current cross-sectional area after necking, or localized narrowing of the specimen.

The original textbook gives the following specimen data: when cast iron elongates by 0.1%, its stress is approximately $8\times10^7$ N/m$^2$.
At the same relative elongation, the stress in steel is $2\times10^7$ N/m$^2$.
These values are retained as printed, but the original numerical dataset and curves have not been quantitatively reconciled or verified as material constants.

This section retains only the textbook's qualitative comparison of brittle and ductile behavior based on these data.
The dataset must not be combined with the previous lesson's Young's modulus example, which describes stiffness in linear elastic tension, to make numerical inferences or derive verified material parameters.

According to the textbook, cast iron fractures at an elongation of 0.45%, with almost no pronounced plastic stage, and its ultimate tensile strength, the maximum engineering stress reached in tension, is $12\times10^7$ N/m$^2$.
The scale near the curve's endpoint is only an approximate illustration and must not be read as a precise value that exactly matches the fracture value in the prose.

The textbook's steel specimen remains elastic at $\varepsilon=0.45\%$ and fractures only at $\varepsilon\approx15\%$, with an ultimate tensile strength of $7\times10^8$ N/m$^2$.
These elastic ranges, fracture elongations, and strengths depend on the particular specimen and experimental conditions.
They must not be combined with the earlier steel example's range to form a universal limit for all steels.
prose.source_text: 利用拉伸时 $\sigma$ 和 $\varepsilon$ 的关系图线，很容易说明脆性物体的特点. 生铁和钢的拉伸图线分别描绘在图89和90上. 从图上可以看出：在拉伸生铁总共只有0.1%时，其中产生的应力约为 $8\times10^7$ 牛顿/米$^2$，钢在相同形变时产生的应力只等于 $2\times10^7$ 牛顿/米$^2$. 当伸长到0.45%时，生铁立刻破裂，几乎没有塑性形变阶段. 它的强度极限等于 $12\times10^7$ 牛顿/米$^2$. 钢在形变 $\varepsilon=0.45\%$ 时仍保持弹性，当 $\varepsilon\approx15\%$ 时才破裂. 钢的强度极限等于 $7\times10^8$ 牛顿/米$^2$.

prose.text:
The cast iron graph emphasizes the absence of a pronounced stage of plastic elongation before fracture.
Other brittle materials may also fracture without noticeable plastic deformation, but how rapidly stress rises with elongation depends on their stiffness and test conditions.

Curves of the same steepness are not a common feature of all brittle materials.
The phrase "almost no plastic deformation" is an approximate description used here to compare brittle and ductile behavior, not a requirement that every brittle material have absolutely no plastic processes under all conditions.
prose.source_text: 不仅生铁，而且所有脆性材料，其应力随着伸长增大得很快. 在形变很小时它们就破裂. 脆性材料实际上没有塑性性质.

prose.text: 任何材料组成的物体，当形变很小时都象弹性体一样，当去掉负载时，它的大小和形状得到恢复. 同时，几乎所有的物体都可以在某种程度上产生塑性形变.
不同材料的力学性质是不同的. 象橡皮或钢这样的材料，当应力和形变比较大时，仍具有弹性性质. 例如，对于钢来说，直到 $\varepsilon=1\%$ 还满足胡克定律，而对于橡皮来说，直到 $\varepsilon$ 相当大，等于百分之几十时，还满足胡克定律. 因此，这些物体叫做弹性物体.

用铁锤很难把冷的钢或铁锻造成形. 但是，把它们加热到很高温度以后，用锻造工具很容易使它们具有任意的形变. 如果把铅冷却到 $-100^\circ C$ 以下，则在室温下为塑性的铅就明显地表现出弹性性质.

不仅生铁，而且所有脆性材料，其应力随着伸长增大得很快. 在形变很小时它们就破裂. 脆性材料实际上没有塑性性质.
